title: Kingslayers — The Frozen Throne Falls
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# 👑 KINGSLAYERS — THE FROZEN THRONE FALLS

We came to Icecrown for one thing: **the Lich King.**

The citadel opened like it knew. The Spire, the Plagueworks, the Crimson Hall, the Frostwing Halls fell one after another, and the swarm reached the top of the world with the night still ahead.

Then we met the king on his throne, and **the night got hard.**

Try after try he threw us off his roof. We changed the plan. And every pull got closer — close enough to taste. Three hours came and went. Midnight too. Any other night, the Rats call it there.

Not this one. In the quietest hour after midnight somebody said it, and ten rats agreed: ***just one more.***

The last stand, the king almost down — and **Grunho**, our Rat King, brimming with a warrior's fury, did what he does best.

He ***charged.*** **Again.** *(The red tide sends its regards.)*

He never saw the frozen orb. His shoulder found it before his eyes did.

It went off like a dying star. Ten rats on the ice. Wipe.

Most guilds call it there. *Next week.* The Rats looked at their king on the floor and said:

**"It's fine, Grunho. We all make mistakes. One more."** 🧀

And every rat on that roof gave the best they had. The dead fell. The winged ones fell. And the king in the frozen crown went down on his own throne — **and did not rise.**

**THE LICH KING IS DEAD.** ❄️💀

Then, as the old rite of the Sewer demands, ten rats took their seats upon the fallen king. Sat. Stood. Sat. Stood. With great respect. Mostly.

Carve these names into the ice forever — **the Kingslayers:** 🐀 **Grunho · Okanor · Rellik · Kobee · Onetreeheals · Shmurda · Lecoque · Tchilly · Cryptwall · Yahmom**

For the Horde. For the cheese. 🐀🧀

*So it is written.*

title: The Hand That Claims Three
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# 🛡️ The Hand That Claims Three

Long ago the Light gave the paladins a gift: lay your hand on a comrade in peril, and the Light turns their attackers upon you.

*Up to three of them.*

The old masters never said **which** three. The Light does not ask. It takes whatever is nearest and most offended, and it takes it *right now*.

**Grunho** learned this the hard way.

On the Frozen Throne the Rat King held the Lich King himself, shield raised, all in order. Then ghouls went loose, and **Mongoloide** reached out to protect a comrade.

Two ghouls turned. And so did Arthas.

The master of the Scourge turned his back on a crowned rat and walked off after a paladin with a hammer, because the paladin wanted ghouls. It happened once. Then again. Mongoloide wanted the ghouls very badly, every time.

Then came yesterday, in the hall of the Blood Princes.

Grunho had them both, Valanar and Taldaram, held tight under the crown. Half a hall away drifted a little dark orb, the sort that floats around Keleseth looking sad. **Rellik** wanted that orb.

The Light looked for three hostile things. It found one small orb.

It also found two princes.

Two lords of the blood crossed the entire hall without a word, to go and stand beside a pebble.

The Rat King looked at his shield, at the empty floor before it, and has since asked the Silver Hand to amend the gift to *"three targets, and NOT the boss."*

The Light does not take requests.

*So it is written.*

title: The Sewer Healer
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# 🧪 The Sewer Healer

The Blood Queen has a cruel sense of humour. She likes to take the Light first.

She marked **Okanor** with her shadows, and the fire began to crawl across the stone behind him. A paladin knows what to do with fire. You walk out of it.

Then she screamed.

Terror. Every rat in the hall lost his legs at once, and the Lightkeeper ran blind, straight back through his own shadow fire. When the fear broke, his mace and his shield were lying on the floor, and the amber runes on his plate had gone dark.

The raid had one healer left. Then the Queen rose into the air.

**Ardil**, the ClawFather, stood under the bolts with his staff raised and his starlight burning. The air phase took him anyway. The starfall went out over the hall, and his spirit-cat faded into the dark.

Then there was one.

**Mijinho**. No armour. A rag around the waist. Eyes too wide. A jar of green sewer brew in one hand that no sane healer would carry into a raid.

He did not panic. He laughed.

The jar came up. The green light poured down over the raid, and the storm answered him from above. Tank, mages, warriors, every rat in the hall drinking from the sewer whether he liked it or not. One healer, one jar, nine bars of health, and a Queen who wanted all of them.

She came down from the air hungry. She found every rat still standing.

And the Blood Queen of Icecrown fell to a raid kept alive by sewer water.

Okanor watched it from the floor. Every rat in the guild owes that shaman a wheel of cheese.

*The Light fell first. The sewer held.*

*So it is written.*

title: The Wrong Target
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# ⚔️ The Wrong Target

For a full turning of the moon the Rats went up the Citadel every single night, and every single night **Rellik** was there — greatsword in both hands, the High Warlord of the front line, cutting a road through the Scourge for everyone behind him.

Then came the alt run, and a strange thought took him. He set the paladin aside, woke his death knight from the cold, and said: *Tonight, I will be the one who holds them.*

The Rats cheered. The Rats should have asked questions.

High above the clouds the two great airships closed on each other, cannon roaring, and it fell to the tank to do the one thing the tank does on that deck: leap the gap, land among the enemy, and seize the dwarf lord at the rail with the grip of the dead. Hold him. Keep his eyes on you and only on you, so he does not walk across and tear the raid apart.

Rellik leapt. Rellik landed. It was a beautiful jump.

And then Rellik turned his back on the dwarf lord entirely and started beating a mage.

On the Horde deck the raid watched the commander stand there, untouched, unbothered, free to do as he pleased. The question went up through the cannon smoke:

*"So... nobody is holding the boss?"*

And from the far deck, calm as a sunrise, came the answer:

*"I'm already hitting the mage."*

It took the High Warlord a long moment to look up from the mage, then over at the dwarf waiting at the edge of the ship, and finally understand what the whole raid had been trying to tell him.

He held the dwarf lord after that. And when the smoke cleared he gave his verdict on the matter, with all the dignity of a month of nightly raiding behind him:

*"I've never tanked this. I don't know."*

A month. Every night. The airship, every night.

The mage, for the record, did not survive. Nobody has ever been so thoroughly hit.

*So it is written.*

title: Came, Feasted, Fled
body:
*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# 🕯️ Came, Feasted, Fled

There is an old curse in the Sewer: *came, feasted, fled.* The rat who walks into the citadel beside you, takes his share of the spoils, and is gone before the torches burn down.

This afternoon it found a Sewer Rat named **Zdral**, a shaman on the lowest rung. He ate at the Rats' table, took what the dead kings dropped, and then the hall heard only this:

*Zdral has left the guild.*

No word. No farewell. Just an empty seat.

Another shaman laughed at the empty seat. **Fazcafe**, who had healed beside the Rats for many seasons, mocked the deserter loudest of all. *Came, feasted, fled,* he sneered.

But the laughter turned to loot — who was owed what, old grudges dragged into the light. For a full hour the argument ran cold through the guild halls while the Rats listened in silence.

And when the last word was spoken, the hall heard it again:

*Ninjacaldas has left the guild.*

The same afternoon. The same plate still warm. The rat who had mocked the deserter walked out through the same door, for the same reason.

Later, **Okanor** stepped into the halls, read the message still hanging in the air, and gave the shaman back his own words: *took the loot and left.*

From somewhere outside the walls came the answer: *"Exactly. Nice conclusion."* And one last sneer: *"Run. You've still got time to kick one."*

Two healers gone before nightfall. Two spirits the Rats had carried through the frozen halls, kept fed, kept geared.

His ancestors stood in the doorway and watched him walk into the snow, and did not follow. The dead remember who stood beside them. They remember who left.

The table is quieter now. The Rats eat in silence, and they count the empty seats.

*A rat who leaves with the loot leaves without his name.*

*So it is written.*

title: The Last Three
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# ⚔️ The Last Three

The Rats climbed to the Frozen Throne and pulled the king **once**. No wipes. No second try. And for a long while it was almost easy. The plan held. The ice held. The king bled slowly, as kings do.

Then came the last phase, and the throne remembered what it was.

The first tank fell. The second took his place, and fell. The king did not hurry. He never needs to. One by one the shields went down on the ice, and behind them the swarm began to thin — a rat here, a rat there, until the roof of the world was mostly silence and frost.

**Fifteen percent.** Three rats still standing.

**Shmurda** was never a tank. He is a warrior of the two-handed blade, built to break things, not to hold them. But there was no one else. So he stepped in front of the Lich King, raised his steel, and *took the king's attention* — and kept it.

**Kobee**, the last blade in the raid, did not look at the bodies or the numbers. Poison, steel, the king's back. Again. Again.

And **Okanor**, the last healer, poured every drop of Light he had left into one warrior who should never have been standing there.

Fourteen. Twelve. The king struck, and Shmurda did not fall. Eleven. The Light held.

**Ten.**

The Lich King stopped. The blade in his hand went still. And the throne that had swallowed a whole raid let go of the last three Rats standing on it.

Seven rats lay on the ice and watched it happen. Nobody spoke. Then everyone did.

*One pull. Three rats. Five percent. One king.*

*So it is written.*

title: Someday and the Frozen King
body:
*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# ❄️ Someday and the Frozen King

Sindragosa. Last phase. The Frost Queen was low, and the rats had done everything right.

Before the pull the raid leader asked once: "Does anyone not know what to do?"

Nobody spoke. Every rat was ready, or so the silence said.

Then the Frost Beacon landed on **Someday**.

The job was simple: walk to the middle and take the Ice Tomb there.

Someday went to the side.

"MIDDLE!" yelled the raid. "Someday, MIDDLE!"

Someday heard it, and Someday acted. He hit **Blink** and went forward, past the middle, right into the front, where the tank was standing.

**Grunho** had a moment to turn his head.

The tomb landed. Two blocks of ice rose side by side: one with a confused mage in it, and one with the Rat King, crown and shield and all, frozen in place in front of the dragon.

Sindragosa looked at her frozen tank. Then she looked at the raid with no tank.

**WIPE.**

The raid leader typed one line in chat:

> "So... nobody had questions?"

That broke the silence. Somebody snorted on voice, then somebody else, and within seconds the whole sewer was laughing: twenty-five rats lying dead on the ice, crying with laughter, while the Rat King thawed out with the look of a man planning a very long talk.

Nobody was angry. It was the best wipe of the night.

Since that night every pull starts the same way. The question is no longer "does anyone not know what to do?" It is: **"Someday, where is the middle?"**

*So it is written.*

title: The Flames Stay With You
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# 🔥 The Flames Stay With You

The clock was still running. Minchar was still in chains. And the Rats had made it — past the hall, past the princes, all the way to the throne of the Blood Queen herself, on **heroic**.

She was almost done. **Thirty percent.** The whole raid stood packed together under her, shoulder to shoulder, because that is how you survive the Queen: her pact chains rats together, and chains only break when the rats stand close. Ten rats, one tight knot. Nobody moves.

Except the one who has to.

Every so often the Queen marks a rat with her shadows. The mark is simple. It burns at your feet, and it follows you. And the law of that fight is simpler still: **you take your fire somewhere else.** You run. Away from the knot, away from your friends, and you leave the flames where they can't hurt anyone.

The shadows found **Rellik**.

And Rellik — High Warlord, Warchief of the Rats, a blade that has cut down kings — was busy. The Queen was at thirty percent. His sword was singing. The numbers were beautiful.

He did not run.

He stood in the very center of the raid, swinging that great golden blade with both hands, and the fire pooled beneath him. Then it spread. Then it was under the healers. Then the tanks. Then everyone.

For a few seconds it was almost peaceful — ten rats, perfectly stacked, perfectly together, perfectly on fire.

The Blood Queen did not even have to bite anyone.

Thirty percent. So close you could taste it.

*The chains say stand together. The fire says stand alone. Learn the difference.*

*So it is written.*

title: The Whole Room
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# 🩸 The Whole Room

Deep in the Crimson Hall, a spy named Minchar hangs in chains, waiting for the Blood Queen to finish him. The Rats were given half an hour. Thirty minutes to cut through her court, kill her princes, kill the queen, and carry him out.

Thirty minutes is not long in the Crimson Hall.

On a normal night the Rats clear those halls the careful way. A stun on one noble. A sheep on another. The archmage held, the tactician held, and the pack taken apart one vampire at a time, like a lock picked pin by pin.

There was no time for locks tonight.

**Okanor** gave the order: *"Be quick. Pull everything."*

Every rat in the raid understood what that meant. One pack. Then the next. No sheep, no stuns, no patience — just speed.

Every rat but one.

**Mongoloide** raised his shield, looked down the length of the Crimson Hall, and heard the word *everything*. And Mongoloide is a rat who takes his orders seriously.

He did not pull the pack.

He pulled **the hall.**

Nobles. Blood knights. Archmages. Tacticians. Fiends. Ten of them, then twelve, then more — the whole court of the San'layn turning at once and coming down the red carpet like a wave of velvet and teeth.

For one long second the raid simply watched it arrive.

Then the healers did the math. Then the mages did the math. Then nobody had to do math anymore, because the floor of the Crimson Hall was covered in Rats.

Somewhere above them, the Blood Queen smiled. Minchar's clock kept ticking.

title: The Dark Two
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# 🩸 The Dark Two

The Blood Queen does not kill you all at once. She takes her time. A bite here, a terror there, and one by one the Rats went down on the cold floor of her hall, until the hall was quiet and the Queen was still flying.

Eight rats on the floor. Two still standing.

Not the tanks. Not the healers. Not the heroes of the Light.

**Foug** — a Death Knight who reads his runes the way other rats read the weather, and who was not tanking anything that night.

And **FranzHerman** — a Warlock who keeps his curses in a book and his demon on a short chain.

Two rats who had spent their whole lives studying the dark. And now they were the only thing left standing between the Queen and a full wipe.

Nobody on the floor said a word. Nobody breathed. Every rat in the raid sat there holding his heart in his hands — and, if we are honest, holding a few other things as well.

The Queen rose into the air. The air phase. The one that kills raids that are *full*. Shadows rained down on two rats.

Foug's ghoul did not stop. Franz's curses did not stop. The runes burned green, the shadows burned violet, and for twenty long seconds the darkness fought the darkness — and the darkness that belonged to the Rats was hungrier.

She came back down. They were still there.

And then the Blood Queen fell to the two least holy creatures in the guild.

The floor of the hall exploded in noise.

*The Light had left the room. It turned out we didn't need it.*

*So it is written.*

title: Grunho and the Red Tide
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# 🧪 Grunho and the Red Tide

High in the frozen citadel, in the laboratory where the mad one works, there is a thing that hunts.

It has no face to strike and no throat to open. It is a red tide in a glass-strewn hall, and it chooses one rat out of all the rats, and it comes for that one and no other. The law of the thing is old and simple, and every Rat who has ever set foot on that filthy floor knows it by heart: **you do not meet it. You run, and you run alone, and you keep the rest of the world behind you.**

**Grunho** has never in his life run from anything.

He saw it turn. He saw it choose. And the Rat King did what the Rat King has done at every door, every bridge and every wall the Rats have ever held — he set his shoulder, he picked his ground, and he *charged* to meet it.

It was, the tome must record, magnificent. For perhaps a heartbeat and a half.

The red tide did not care that he was a king. It did not care about the crown, or the shield, or the long red cloak, or the twenty-four other rats standing in a tidy little cluster directly behind him exactly where he had told them to stand. It took him, and then — being a tide — it took everything he was standing in front of.

The laboratory was quiet after that. The mad one above did not even look up.

They speak of it still. Not as a defeat. As a **blast**.

Let it be written plainly, so that no future rat mistakes the lesson: the Rat King has held every wall worth holding. He has held doors that should not have held. He will hold them again.

He has, however, been formally excused from holding back a puddle.

*So it is written.*

title: When the Gate Learned to Choose
body:
*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# ⚔️ When the Gate Learned to Choose

The Fangs were never a prize. They were a solution to a scheduling problem.

In the old halls the difficulty was chosen at the door. A raid went in hard or it went in soft, and that choice bound every rat inside it for the whole night. But the swarm had never wanted one thing. Some rats came to grind the hard modes until the mechanics broke. Others came to clear, to gear, to farm and go to bed. Both were right. Neither could have the night.

So the Warchief drew a tier — the Fangs — and it meant something plain: these are the rats who signed for the hard way. Not better. *Willing.* It let the guild field a hard-mode roster without dragging anyone into a wall they never asked for, and it let the rest raid in peace. It was a workaround, and it worked.

Then came Icecrown.

And Icecrown does not ask at the door. It asks at every boss. The same raid, the same night, the same rats — and the choice made fresh at each gate. Hard where the swarm has the appetite for it. Straight through where it doesn't. One roster, deciding as it goes.

The problem the Fangs were built to solve simply stopped existing.

So the tier came down, for the reason any good tool is put away: the job is done. No roster to keep separate, no second ladder to tend, no rat sorted by which difficulty they prefer. The willing and the steady raid the same night now, and Icecrown sorts it boss by boss.

Three ranks remain: the sewer, the raiders, and the Warchiefs who lead them.

The gate chooses now. We just show up.

*Set down in the Chronicles of the Sewer.*

title: The Five-Day Exile of Grunho
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# ⚖️ The Five-Day Exile of the Rat King

There came a day when **Grunho** — he who has held the line at the front of every wall the Rats ever stood behind — went down into a lesser dark with strangers at his back.

He was a shield-bearer. He had always been a shield-bearer. But the axe that fell from that hollow was no shield-bearer's axe, and the Rat King has never pretended to be a humble creature.

So he did the honourable thing. **He spoke first.**
Before the roll, before the axe was even cold, he told them plainly: *I am taking this one as a warrior takes it, not as a guardian.* No trickery. No silence. No hand slipped into another rat's satchel while the torches were low.

And the dice fell, and they fell for him.

It was then that the Wardens came.

Not the Scourge. Not the Legion. Something colder and infinitely more petty — the faceless ones who watch from outside the world, who do not raid, who have never held a wall, who read a single line of a report and render judgement without ever once asking what was said aloud before the roll.

**Five days**, they decreed. Five days cast out of the world.

The Rat King did not argue. Kings do not argue with clerks.
He hung the tower shield on the wall, set the iron crown down beside it, and sat out the sentence in the dark with the patience of something that knows it will still be here long after the Wardens have moved on to bother somebody else.

The axe is still his. The ruling changed nothing but the calendar.

Five days is nothing. He has held doors longer than that.

*So it is written.*

title: A Tribute to Insanity — First Full ToGC 10-Man Clear
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# 🏆 A TRIBUTE TO INSANITY

**Tirion built a coliseum to find out who is worthy to march on the Lich King. Tonight ten rats walked in to answer him. 🐀**

The beasts of Northrend came first, out of the cold and the deep sand. Then a gnome reached past his grasp and let a **pit-lord of the Burning Legion** onto the floor. Then the Crusade sent living champions — the only enemy in that place that could think. Every door opened, and every door closed behind us. 💀

Then the **Val'kyr** came on Arthas' errand, and we understood he had been watching the whole time.

When the trial was nearly done, **the Lich King took the floor out from under us.** Down in the dark beneath the arena **Anub'arak** was waiting — his own general, sent up through the ice to end us before we ever reached his gates.

**He is still down there. We are not.** 🕷️

The Crusade counts. Fifty times that coliseum was willing to watch us fall, and the whole arena counts with it. **It never got to start.**

So they brought out the chest they took off the **Black Knight** — Arthas' own spy, planted in the tournament and put in the ground for it — and the Crusade handed his spoils to ten rats from the sewer. 🏆

They have a name in that place for those who go in and never once go down. It is not meant kindly.

**We were insane. And we won.** 🐀🧀

title: The Beasts and the Pit-Lord Fall — First Heroic ToC
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# 🩸 TWO FALL IN THE COLISEUM — FIRST HEROIC NIGHT

**Tonight the sand ran red, and it was not ours. 🐀**

We walked into the **Crusaders' Coliseum** on the hard road — the **Heroic** trial, the one that does not forgive — and we walked in **short.** Raiders scattered to the wind, on leave and away, the pack thinned to the bone. So thin we opened the gate and let **two strays** run with the swarm to fill the line. Not one Rat flinched, and the strays held right alongside them.

**Tirion** opened the gate, and the **Beasts of Northrend** came. First **Gormok** the impaler. Then the great worms out of the deep, **Acidmaw** and **Dreadscale**. And last the mountain himself, **Icehowl**, who lowered his horns and charged the whole pack at once. A long, grinding hold — blades not lowering, healers running dry and refusing to fall — and when the last beast went down into the bloodied sand, **the swarm was still standing.** 💀

But the Coliseum was not done asking. Beyond the churned floor a second door burned open. A gnome named **Wilfred Fizzlebang** reached beyond his grasp, and through the portal stepped no servant — **Lord Jaraxxus**, pit-lord of the Burning Legion, a general who had never once feared a rat.

He met this swarm short-handed and bleeding. He scattered his fel-fire across the sand and called his mistresses out of the flame — and **the thin line held, and closed, and pulled him down too.** 🔥

Two Heroic kills in one night. Fewer of us than ever. **First Heroic night in the book — and it was a double.**

They built this coliseum to find who is worthy to march on the Lich King. Tonight, short-handed and unbroken, **the Sewer answered twice.**

🔥 **BEASTS DOWN. PIT-LORD DOWN. LONG LIVE RATS.** 🔥

For the Horde. For the cheese. 🐀🧀

title: The Trial of the Crusader
body:
@everyone

*From the Chronicles of the Sewer...*

# ⚔️ THE RATS ANSWER THE CALL — TRIAL OF THE CRUSADER

**Today, the gate opens. 🐀**

**Tirion Fordring** raised the Argent Crusade upon the ice of Icecrown and built a coliseum in the Lich King's own shadow — and there he asks every would-be champion one question before they dare march on the Frozen Throne: **are you worthy?**

Today he asks it of the **Rats**.

We are no highborn champions. We are the **rats of the Dalaran sewers** — the swarm that boiled up out of the drains, tore through **Naxxramas**, and brought down the titan-halls of **Ulduar**. And now, out of every grate and shadow beneath this coliseum, **the swarm rises again.** At the front stand the hardest of the pack, blades lit and shields raised. Behind them — **all of us.** **Garrosh** himself leans forward on his seat to watch.

They used to laugh at the gutter-rats. They stopped laughing somewhere between Naxxramas and Ulduar.

Because beyond that gate the trial is waiting. The **beasts of Northrend** paw the sand. The pit-lord **Jaraxxus** coils in his portal. The **twin Val'kyr** take their marks, and far below, the traitor **Anub'arak** presses his ear to the floor — listening for the tread of fools.

**He is going to hear us coming.** 💀

No crown. No bloodline. Just teeth, steel, and a whole swarm that refuses to kneel.

So sharpen your fangs and get to the gate. **This is the night the coliseum learns our name.**

The Crusade asks who is worthy to march on the Lich King.

🔥 **TONIGHT, THE SEWER ANSWERS.** 🔥

For the Horde. For the cheese. **LONG LIVE RATS.** 🐀🧀

# 🌊 The Turning of Ninjacaldas

For many seasons **Ninjacaldas** kept the Rats alive as a druid of the wild. He walked in the shape of the great tree, roots sunk deep, and drew on the Emerald Dream to knit flesh whole and drag the fallen back to their feet. When the swarm should have wiped, Ninjacaldas held them — patient, rooted, unmoving. Where he stood, rats did not stay dead.

But the Dream is a slow and sleeping thing, and Ninjacaldas had begun to hear a wilder voice — the raw call of Azeroth herself, older than any grove.

So he shed the bark and the antlers and climbed to where the elements still speak plainly. He raised the totems upon the bare stone, and water, earth, air and fire took his measure and found him worthy. The ancestors leaned close — for here was a rat who had spent a lifetime learning to give, and the spirits know their own.

He heals still. He was always a healer. He simply calls upon the elements now, where once he called upon the Dream.

The Emerald Dream is quieter for his leaving. The Maelstrom churns a little louder.

*So it is written.*

title: The Forging of Val'anyr
body:
🐀 **VAL'ANYR — HAMMER OF ANCIENT KINGS** 🐀

Long before the swarm, the **titan-keepers** forged a hammer of pure creation and set it in the hands of the **kings of the earthen**, deep beneath Ulduar. With it those ancient kings mended their own — **sealing wound and stone alike**, a weapon made not to slay but to **make whole**. Then the **curse of flesh** took the earthen, the kings fell to ruin, and **Val'anyr shattered** — scattered through the titan-halls, its light gone dark for **ten thousand years**. 🧀

For **three months** the RATS came for it.

Night after night we poured into Ulduar — through **Freya's grove**, **Mimiron's fire**, **Thorim's storm**, down into the pit where the **Old God** whispers. Every night the swarm dragged **one more fragment** home in its teeth. Fragment by fragment the Hammer came together in **Okanor's claws**.

And today — **the last shard fell into place.** :boom:

At the titans' own altar the **Hammer WOKE**. Gold light spilled out after ten thousand years of silence, and **Val'anyr was whole again.**

Not in the hand of a titan. Not in the hand of a king.

**In the claws of a rat.** ⚒️🔥

*A legendary — forged by the swarm, for the swarm. Three months. One Hammer. Ours.*

Long live RATS. 🐀🧀

title: The Long Night of the Chained Drake
body:
*From the Chronicles of the Sewer, as told by the Loremaster of RATS...*

# ⚒️ The Long Night of the Chained Drake ⚒️

Razorscale did not fall easily. She never does.

Bound in her pit by iron chains, the great proto-drake screamed fire across the Antechamber while the Watchers of Ulduar marched endlessly from the dark — iron dwarves without number, hammers raised, eyes like cold forge-light.

The Rats had not come merely to kill her. They had come for the harder thing — the deed the scribes call *achievement* — and that meant the dwarves had to die. All twenty-five of them, cut down amid the harpoons and the falling flame, in the narrow space between one breath of fire and the next.

The first wipe came fast. So did the second. And the third.

The pit filled with their dead and emptied again as they returned, and returned, and returned. Harpoons missed. A drake grounded too soon. A dwarf left standing when the timer bled out. Each failure a fresh bruise.

A lesser warband would have called the ID and gone to bed. The Rats did not.

They learned the rhythm of it — who held the line, who struck the chains, who counted the dwarves aloud in the chaos. Wipe by wipe the war tightened, until at last the twenty-fifth iron body hit the stone and Razorscale crashed down with it.

Exhausted. Repair-poor. Victorious.

The achievement was theirs — earned the only way the Rats ever earn anything. The hard way.

*— The Loremaster*

title: The Madness in the Brain of Yogg-Saron
body:
*From the Chronicles of the Sewer, as told by the Loremaster of RATS...*

# 🩸 The Madness in the Brain of Yogg-Saron 🩸

It came in the second phase, as it always does — when the floor opened and the portals yawned wide, beckoning the bravest into the mind of the Old God itself.

And so the Warchief's Fangs went in. Down into the brain room, into the whispering dark, where the walls breathe and reason rots.

But the Fangs did not look at the tentacles. They looked back — through the rift, out onto the raid floor — and what they saw was death. Rat after rat, falling. A pile of the fallen growing higher with every breath.

The Sanity of the Fangs drained like blood from a wound.

The whispers grew louder. *Look what they've done. Look how they die without you.* And something in the Fangs — something tired, something laughing — agreed.

They came back through the portal not as saviours, but as servants of the madness. Eyes empty. Blades turned the wrong way.

And the Fangs fell upon their own.

It was not a wipe of failure. It was a wipe of comedy — the protectors of the guild, mind-broken, gleefully cutting down every last rat they had sworn to defend. The raid ended in laughter and ash.

Yogg-Saron won that night. But the legend was the Fangs', and it will be told for as long as rats remember how to laugh at their own ruin.

*— The Loremaster*

title: A Soul Reforged
body:
# ❄️ A Soul Reforged ❄️

For years, **Nutelaa** walked the dark path of the Warlock — commanding demons, wielding shadow and flame, leaving ruin in her wake across every raid the Rats have ever set foot in.

But the sewer calls for more than shadow.

It calls for frost.

Without hesitation, without being asked, she shed her dark pact. Dismissed her demons one last time. And stepped into the cold.

From the ashes of the Warlock...

A Death Knight was born.

Twin axes in hand, frost runes burning blue, she now walks a harder path — and she walks it for us.

🧊 **Nutelaa** has risen. Frost Death Knight of the Rats.

May Icecrown tremble at what approaches.
